messages:

Subject: MAP: reconcile prefetch + batching assumptions for unit-econ close

Hi Elena / PilotHealth team —

As we get this MAP into the final sprint, we need to lock the unit-econ assumptions that feed the SOW and pricing appendix. To avoid last-minute surprises during procurement, can we align on the following items this week? I attached a working spreadsheet (prefetch_model_profile.xlsx) with the fields we need to finalize.

Key asks (short):
- Tokens per user flow (median + 95th percentile) — we currently model 850 median / 2,700 p95 for the triage flow.
- KV/prefix caching hit rate assumption — our default MAP template uses 25% but the pilot traffic you shared in discovery looked more cache-friendly.
- Batching target / max latency window — we model a 12ms incremental per-token cost at 8-request batching; we need to confirm acceptable tail latency if we increase batching to 16.
- Prefetch strategy: which prompts are safe to prefetch/execute server-side vs on-demand? That changes tokens/$ materially.

Why this matters: small changes to caching hit rate or prefetch coverage alter tokens-per-session by ~15–30% in our sensitivity table. We want to lock assumptions before the procurement SOW and before we produce the final units-per-dollar table for finance.

Proposed timeline: please confirm numbers or share PilotHealth traffic/export by EOD Wed (19 Aug). If needed, we can run a short simulated pass on our side against the sample CSV — Ben can run the sensitivity sweep and return the delta to the MAP.

Attachment: prefetch_model_profile.xlsx (input cells highlighted).

Thanks —
Michael

Subject: Re: MAP: reconcile prefetch + batching assumptions for unit-econ close

Thanks Michael —

Appreciate the clarity. Quick answers and a few follow-ups: we attached a small traffic export (pilot_traffic_profile.csv).

- Tokens per flow: our product analytics shows 760 median / ~2,100 p95 for the triage path you described (we can export more samples if you need).
- Caching: we have a server-side cache for previous clinician notes; rough hit rate today is ~32% for identical prompts but degrades across multi-user sessions. We can agree to a conservative 25–30% for the MAP but would like Redwood to show the sensitivity at 20/30/40%.
- Batching: our SLAs are strict on tail latency — 99th must be <250ms for live triage. We can accept short batching windows if end-to-end 99th stays within 250ms.
- Prefetch: we're comfortable prefetching prompt #1 and #3 in the flow but not patient-identifying content until after consent.

We'll review your spreadsheet later today and aim to confirm by Wed. If you have a simple sensitivity report (20/30/40% cache hit), that will help procurement signoff.

Elena Cruz
Head of Integrations, PilotHealth
elena@pilothealth.com

Michael / team / Elena —

I ran a quick sweep against the pilot_traffic_profile.csv Elena provided. Attached is a short sensitivity workbook (prefetch_model_profile.xlsx, tab: sensitivity). High-level:

- Baseline (our current MAP template): 25% cache hit, batching at 8 requests => 0.65 tokens/session delta vs raw token count (after typical prompt compression).
- If cache hit = 20% => tokens/session +11% relative to baseline. If cache hit = 40% => tokens/session -14% relative to baseline.
- Prefetching prompt #1 and #3 reduces median tokens/session by ~9% in the simulated flows; combined with a 30% cache hit this nets ~20% lower tokens/$ than the conservative MAP model.
- Batching increase to 16 (keeping same batching latency target) lowers per-token cost by ~6% but adds ~30–40ms p50 and ~80–120ms p95. For PilotHealth's 99th <250ms constraint, there's headroom but we should cap batching to 12 for live triage to be safe.

I've annotated the workbook with the cells we need Elena/Procurement to confirm (tokens median/p95, acceptable batching cap for live triage flow, and prefetch consent list).

Attachment: prefetch_model_profile.xlsx (tab: sensitivity).

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
